3. In order to import pharmaceutical raw materials namely "metronidazole", the petitioner obtained approval of a "block list" for its price from the drug Admin Authority as per terms of the order being SRO No. 103-law/98 dated 10.6.98. The said block list prices were approved on the condition that the petitioner would not be required to obtain any further approval if they import raw materials on a price lower than the listed price. A copy of the said block list dated 23.2.99 is annexed to the petition and marked as Annexure-A. Thereafter the petitioner opened an L.C. being No. 2531/155/11.99 dated 3.3.99 through Agrani Bank, Ramna, Corporate Branch, 18 B.B. Avenue, Dhaka for importing 3000 kgs of metronidazole under H.S. Code No. 2933, 29.00 at the rate of US$ 5.50 per Kg. which was lower than the listed price i.e. US$ 5.50 per Kg. which was lower than the listed price i.e. US$ 5.95 per kgs. The petitioner obtained approval of the said import price from the concerned authority on 9.3.99, copies of the said letter of credit dated 3.3.99 and the approval letter dated 9.3.99 are annexed to the petitioner and marked as Annexure-B and C respectively. After arrival of the said goods at Chittagong Port, the petitioner submitted Bill of Entry being No. C 35471 dated 6.5.99 to release the goods on payment of Customs duty, VAT and other charges on the basis of invoice value. After receiving the said Bill of Entry the Customs Authority initiated a file bearing Nothi No. 540/AP/Group-11/98-99 dated 6.5.99 and finally directed to assess the imported goods on the basis of recorded price at the rate of US$ 9.00 per kg instead of in-voice value by the impugned order dated 20.4.99. Being aggrieved the petitioner moved this Court submitting, amongst others, that the fixation of value on the goods and order for assessment of the imported goods on the basis of the said arbitrary and discriminatory value pursuant to an order of an office executive is wholly arbitrary in as much as the petitioner is entitled to pay duties and taxes on the said imported goods at a rate which would reflect the fair price of the goods I the international market and the price of the approved block list by the Drug Administration Authority and not at a grossly inflated and arbitrarily determined value which pre-dates the assessment date by more than 6(six) months and would have no nexus with the price charged ordinarily in course of international trade and the type of goods and Section 25 of the Customs Act does not authorize the respondents to fix such recorded price in as much as the same is arbitrary. Section 25 clearly envisages assessment on the value to be determined under section 25(1), or 25(7) or 25A in respect of the imported goods known as normal value, Tariff Value, CRF value respectively, Apart from those as special case the imported goods refer in reference is valued as per approved block list value duly republished in the Gazette notification under Article 24(3) of the import policy order issued under section 3(1) of the imports and exports (Control) Act, 1950. There is no provision for determination of any "recorded value" by an executive. 

 5. Mr. Shiekh Fazle Noor Tapash with Mr. Mohammad Mehedi Hasan Chowdhury Mr. A.K.M. Rabiul Hassan, the learned Advocates appearing for the petitioner drawing our attention to the provisions as laid down in Article 24(3) of the Imports Policy Order 1997-2002 issued under Section 3(1) of the imports and exports (Control) Act, 1950, which runs as follows:- 

 7. From careful scrutiny of the provision as laid down under Article 24(3) of the Import Policy Order 1997-2002 issued under Section 3(1) of the Imports and Exports (Control) Act 1950, it appears that in case of importation of a pharmaceuticals raw materials, it requires an approval of a "Block list" determining its price from the Drug Admin Authority and the Customs duty and other charges are to be assessed on that price as per approved "Block list" by the Drug Admin Authority. 

 8. Thus in view of the provision laid down as stated above under Article 24(3) of the Import Policy Order 1997-2002 issued under section 3(1) of the Imports and Exports (control) Act 1950, the petitioners obtained approval from the Drug administration Authority of a block list determining its price of Pharmaceutical raw materials before opening an L.C. for importing of the aforesaid consignment as it appears from the Annexure-A and thereafter opened an L.C. and placed the invoice value of the imported goods at the rate of US$ 5.50 per Kg as per approved block list. The petitioner obtained further approval of the import price from the concerned authority on 9.3.99 as evidenced from Annexure —C of the writ petition.
